sentences.text: Office objections are overruled.
Learned High Court Government Pleader takes notice for respondent No.1-State.
Sri. Dr.J.S.Halashetti, learned counsel undertake to appear for respondent No.2.

This petition is filed by petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 4 under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C for quashing criminal proceedings in C.C.51970/2019 arising out of crime No.528/2018 registered by Jeevan Bheemanagar police and charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 504, 498A,
506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

During the pendency of the petition, both petitioner and respondent No.2 appeared through their counsels and filed a joint compromise application along with affidavit under Section 320 read with Section 482 of I.P.C for seeking permission to compound the offence.

It is submitted that divorce has already been granted by the Family Court, permanent alimony of Rs.8,00,000/- has been fixed,
and Rs. 4,00,000/- has already been paid, and today the petitioner is handing over the remaining Rs.4,00,000/- through DD to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 present before this Court and submits that she has received the entire alimony amount.

In view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Gian Singh vs State of Punjab and another (2012) 10 SCC 303, the parties are settled their issues and the Court can quash the criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Gian Singh vs State of Punjab and another (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, I.A.No.2/2023 is allowed.
Parties are permitted to compound the offences.
Consequently, criminal petition is allowed.
The criminal proceedings against petitioner Nos.1 to 4 in C.C.51970/2019 pending on the file of 10th Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru is hereby quashed.
